Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-26", "title": "Cholesterol", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that's found in all the cells in your body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your body needs some cholesterol to make hormones , vitamin D , and substances that help you digest foods."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your body makes all the cholesterol it needs."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Cholesterol is also found in foods from animal sources, such as egg yolks, meat, and cheese."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "If you have too much cholesterol in your blood, it can combine with other substances in the blood to form plaque."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Plaque sticks to the walls of your arteries."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This buildup of plaque is known as atherosclerosis ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "It can lead to coronary artery disease , a condition in which your coronary arteries become narrow or even blocked."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "They are a combination of fat (lipid) and protein."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The lipids need to be attached to the proteins so they can move through the blood."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Different types of lipoproteins have different purposes: HDL stands for high-density lipoprotein."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It is sometimes called \"good\" cholesterol because it helps your body get rid of cholesterol."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It carries cholesterol from other parts of your body back to your liver."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Your liver then removes the cholesterol from your body."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "It is sometimes called \"bad\" cholesterol because a high LDL level leads to the buildup of plaque in your arteries."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "VLDL stands for very low-density lipoprotein."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Some people also call VLDL a \"bad\" cholesterol because it too contributes to the buildup of plaque in your arteries."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "But VLDL and LDL are different; VLDL mainly carries triglycerides and LDL mainly carries cholesterol."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The most common cause of high cholesterol is an unhealthy lifestyle."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "This can include: Unhealthy eating habits, such as eating lots of saturated fats ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "These fats are found in red meats, full-fat dairy products, chocolate, some baked goods, and many deep-fried and processed foods."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Eating too much saturated fat can raise your LDL (bad) cholesterol."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Lack of physical activity , with lots of sitting and little exercise."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "This lowers your HDL (good) cholesterol."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Smoking , which lowers HDL cholesterol, especially in women."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Stress , which may raise levels of certain hormones such as corticosteroids."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "These can cause your body to make more cholesterol."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Drinking too much alcohol , which can raise your total cholesterol level."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Genetics may also cause people to have high cholesterol."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "For example, familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is an inherited condition that causes very high levels of cholesterol in the blood."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Other medical conditions and certain medicines may also raise LDL cholesterol levels or lower HDL cholesterol levels."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "What can raise my risk of high cholesterol?"}, {"id": "S032", "text": "A variety of things can raise your risk of high cholesterol: Age."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Your cholesterol levels tend to rise as you get older."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Even though it is less common, younger people, including children and teens , can also have high cholesterol."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Between ages 20 and 39, men have a greater risk of high total cholesterol than women."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "But after menopause , a woman's risk goes up."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "This happens because menopause lowers levels of female hormones that may protect against high blood cholesterol."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "High blood cholesterol can run in families."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Conditions such as diabetes , chronic kidney disease , HIV , and lupus can raise your risk of high cholesterol."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Certain medicines can raise your level of LDL cholesterol or lower your level of HDL cholesterol, including: Steroids Some chemotherapy medicines Medicines taken after an organ transplant Medicines for certain heart conditions Certain acne medicines Race or ethnicity."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "People from certain racial or ethnic groups may have an increased risk of high cholesterol."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "For example, Asian Americans are more likely to have high levels of LDL cholesterol than other groups."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "And non-Hispanic White people are more likely than other groups to have high levels of total cholesterol."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Being overweight or having obesity raises your cholesterol level."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "What other health problems can high cholesterol cause?"}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Undiagnosed or untreated high blood cholesterol can lead to serious health problems: If you have large deposits of plaque in your arteries, an area of plaque can rupture (break open)."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "This can cause a blood clot to form on the surface of the plaque."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "If the clot becomes large enough, it can mostly or completely block blood flow in a coronary artery."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "If the flow of oxygen-rich blood to your heart muscle is reduced or blocked, it can cause angina (chest pain) or a heart attack ."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Plaque also can build up in other arteries in your body, including the arteries that bring oxygen-rich blood to your brain and limbs."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "This can lead to problems such as carotid artery disease , stroke , and peripheral arterial disease ."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "There are usually no signs or symptoms that you have high cholesterol."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "A blood test can measure your cholesterol levels ."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "When and how often you should get this test depends on your age, risk factors, and family history."}, {"id": "S055", "text": "The general recommendations are: For people who are age 19 or younger: The first test should be between ages 9 to 11 Children should have the test again every 5 years Some children may have this test starting at age 2 if there is a family history of high blood cholesterol, heart attack, or stroke For people who are ages 20 to 65: Younger adults should have the test every 5 years Men ages 45 to 65 and women ages 55 to 65 should have it every 1 to 2 years For people over age 65: They should be tested every year How can I lower my cholesterol?"}, {"id": "S056", "text": "You can lower your cholesterol through heart-healthy lifestyle changes."}, {"id": "S057", "text": "They include a heart-healthy eating plan , weight management , and regular physical activity ."}, {"id": "S058", "text": "If the lifestyle changes alone do not lower your cholesterol enough, you may also need to take medicines."}, {"id": "S059", "text": "There are several types of cholesterol-lowering medicines available, including statins ."}, {"id": "S060", "text": "If you take medicines to lower your cholesterol, you still should continue with the lifestyle changes."}, {"id": "S061", "text": "Some people with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) may receive a treatment called lipoprotein apheresis."}, {"id": "S062", "text": "This treatment uses a filtering machine to remove LDL cholesterol from the blood."}, {"id": "S063", "text": "Then the machine returns the rest of the blood back to the person."}, {"id": "S064", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1656", "title": "Plague", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Plague is an infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The bacteria are found mainly in rats and in the fleas that feed on them."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "People and other animals can get plague from rat or flea bites."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "In the past, plague destroyed entire civilizations."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Today plague is uncommon, due to better living conditions and antibiotics."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "There are three forms of plague: Bubonic plague causes the tonsils, adenoids, spleen, and thymus to become inflamed."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Symptoms include fever, aches, chills, and tender lymph glands."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "In septicemic plague, bacteria multiply in the blood."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It causes fever, chills, shock, and bleeding under the skin or other organs."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Pneumonic plague is the most serious form."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Bacteria enter the lungs and cause pneumonia."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "People with the infection can spread this form to others."}]}, {"id": "MLP-4746", "title": "Hay Fever", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Each spring, summer, and fall, trees, weeds, and grasses release tiny pollen grains into the air."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Some of the pollen ends up in your nose and throat."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "This can trigger a type of allergy called hay fever."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Symptoms can include: Sneezing, often with a runny or clogged nose Coughing and postnasal drip Itching eyes, nose and throat Red and watery eyes Dark circles under the eyes Your health care provider may diagnose hay fever based on a physical exam and your symptoms."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Taking medicines and using nasal sprays can relieve symptoms."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You can also rinse out your nose, but be sure to use distilled or sterilized water with saline."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Allergy shots can help make you less sensitive to pollen and provide long-term relief."}]}, {"id": "MLP-143", "title": "Ankylosing Spondylitis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis of the spine."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It causes inflammation (swelling) between your vertebrae (the bones that make up your spine) and the joints between your spine and pelvis."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "AS inflammation can cause stiffness and make it difficult to move and bend."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Symptoms of AS can range from mild to severe back pain."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Over time, AS can fuse (grow together) your vertebrae, limiting movement and causing a hunched posture."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "In some people, AS can affect other joints or body parts."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "There is no cure for AS, but early treatment can help manage symptoms, slow down the disease, and help you lead a more productive life."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Who is more likely to get ankylosing spondylitis?"}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Ankylosing spondylitis usually starts before age 45."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Early symptoms may begin between the ages of 15 and 30."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Your chance of developing AS can also increase if: You're a man."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If a member of your family has AS, you're more likely to get the disease."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You have other medical conditions that may increase your risk of getting AS."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "These include Crohn's disease , ulcerative colitis , or psoriasis ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "No one knows what causes ankylosing spondylitis, but the environment and genes likely play a role."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Your genes are parts of DNA in your cells that are passed down from your parents."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Certain genes may increase your risk of getting the disease, but not everyone with these genes gets AS."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What are the symptoms of ankylosing spondylitis?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The most common symptom is pain and stiffness in the lower back and/or hips."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The pain is usually worse during the night or after sitting for a long time."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Over time, AS may progress to other areas of your spine or body."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Symptoms may depend on which areas of your body the disease affects."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Some people have symptoms that come and go."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Other symptoms of ankylosing spondylitis may include: Pain, stiffness, and inflammation of the joints."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "This could occur if the joints connecting the ribs are affected."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Abdominal (belly) pain and loose stools (poop)."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "How is ankylosing spondylitis diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "There is no single test for ankylosing spondylitis."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "To find out if you have AS your health care provider may: Ask about your medical history , including your symptoms."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Ask about your family health history , including relatives who have had AS."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "What are the treatments for ankylosing spondylitis?"}, {"id": "S031", "text": "AS has no cure, but treatment may help relieve symptoms, maintain posture, and slow down the disease."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Since other parts of your body can be affected by AS, you will likely work with a team of health care professionals for tests, diagnosis, and care."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Treatment usually includes medicine to help relieve symptoms and keep the disease from getting worse, as well as physical therapy to improve mobility."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "You can help manage your AS symptoms if you: Exercise Monitor your symptoms Manage your stress Use assistive devices as needed Follow a healthy diet Stop smoking , or don't start NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Disease"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1535", "title": "Child Dental Health", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Healthy teeth are important to your child's overall health."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "From the time your child is born, there are things you can do to promote healthy teeth and prevent cavities ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "For babies, you should clean teeth with a soft, clean cloth or baby's toothbrush."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Avoid putting the baby to bed with a bottle and check teeth regularly for spots or stains."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "For all children, you should: Start using a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste when they are two years old."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You might start sooner, if a dentist or doctor suggests it."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Provide healthy foods and limit sweet snacks and drinks Schedule regular dental check-ups Forming good habits at a young age can help your child have healthy teeth for life."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research"}]}]
